claim.text: Is the statement described in this narrative hearsay under FRE 801(c)?

arguments.text: Sean's call to his lawyer constitutes an out-of-court statement, satisfying the first prong of the FRE 801(c) hearsay definition.
arguments.legal_rule: FRE 801(c) defines hearsay as a statement made outside of the current trial or hearing.

arguments.text: The call is offered to prove the truth of the matter asserted, namely that Sean knew he was going to die, satisfying the second prong of FRE 801(c).
arguments.legal_rule: FRE 801(c) requires the statement to be offered to prove the truth of the matter asserted.
arguments.evidence_span: On the issue of whether Sean knew he was going to die

arguments.text: The evidence is circumstantial conduct (calling a lawyer to change a will) rather than a direct assertion of impending death. Non-assertive conduct offered to prove state of mind is not hearsay under FRE 801(a)(2).
arguments.legal_rule: FRE 801(a)(2) excludes conduct not intended as an assertion from the definition of a statement.
arguments.evidence_span: the fact that he called his lawyer wanting to make final changes to his will

arguments.text: The statement may be offered for a non-hearsay purpose, such as to show the effect on the listener or as a verbal act in will drafting, rather than to prove the truth of the matter asserted.
arguments.legal_rule: Statements offered for purposes other than proving the truth of the matter asserted (e.g., effect on listener, verbal act) fall outside FRE 801(c).
arguments.evidence_span: wanting to make final changes to his will
